quote: I know they're very expensive. So if if this is gonna be very expensive, you could just take me off the list.
stewart_read: Textbook trigger for the 'it's too expensive' flip ('what's expensive is NOT switching') but rep instead pitches no-upfront-cost as a feature.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep could be strategically avoiding argument by reassuring first before pivoting later, but no later pivot to the bill-as-villain reframe ever occurs.
coaching_implication: Coach the flip: use her own $300 bill number (captured minutes later) as the 'expensive' thing, not the panels.

quote: Yeah. And it was I remember it being very, very expensive.
stewart_read: Second touch of the same cost objection; rep responds with generic 'technology has improved' instead of connecting to her current bill pain.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep may be deliberately building rapport before circling back to numbers, but the call ends without ever circling back.
coaching_implication: This was the moment to say 'that's exactly why — most people say the same thing until they see today's numbers against what they're paying now.'

stewart_read: Bill captured but rep files it ('That is good to know') and never reflects it back to create pull toward the appointment.
coaching_implication: Should have used the $300 figure to build curiosity: 'let's see what we could get that down to' — a specific hook, not a filed data point.

quote: the only thing I'll need from you, Donna, is just a copy of your kilowatt usage.
stewart_read: Minor scope creep — rep explains panel-sizing rationale in technical terms rather than staying purely on scheduling logistics.
alternative_hypothesis: Could be read as normal Verify/bill_collection framing rather than true scope creep, since it's part of the standard ask.
coaching_implication: Keep bill-ask framing shorter; the design rationale is closer-tier content.

quote: you have some trees on the southern side of your home. Are all of those trees still there?
stewart_read: Standard Verify-style shading question handled cleanly and briefly — good example of efficient qualification chat.
coaching_implication: No action needed — good pacing here, contrast with the missed flips.

quote: I'll I'll I'll hear from you on Monday. Right? Give me a call on Monday if you if you get a chance.
stewart_read: Call ends with the CUSTOMER proposing the follow-up and the rep agreeing loosely ('sometimes I forget') instead of the rep owning a locked callback time or appointment.
coaching_implication: Rep should have said 'Let's lock in Monday at [time] — I'll call you then' and treated it as an owned appointment, not a maybe.
